newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Ringgit falls back as dollar/majors recover.
newsitem.headline: Ringgit falls back as dollar/majors recover.

text.p: The ringgit fell back against the dollar as dollar/majors recovered on short-covering, but trading remained thin throughout due to lack of participation, dealers said.

They said ringgit was expected to remain in a range in the near-term unless there was sharp movement in dollar/majors, adding that most corporate players have already covered positions for the year-end.
"Unless something major happens, we don't see the ringgit moving out of its recent range. Volume has been very thin," said a dealer with a foreign bank in Kuala Lumpur.
Dealers said given the lack of fresh leads in the market, the ringgit was merely following the movements in dollar/majors.
Fears of a rise in interest rates by the Bank of Japan had earlier pressured the dollar lower against major currencies.
Dealers added that the U.S. November consumer price index (CPI), due out at 1330 GMT today, is unlikely to have much influence on the direction of the dollar.
At 0900 GMT, the ringgit was at 2.5225/35 a dollar against 2.5220/30 at the close of Kuala Lumpur on Wednesday. It hit a high of 2.5195/00 in early trading.
